title: Measuring Claim-to-Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1‑2026‑08‑26) that measured the fraction of LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals that would produce unsafe simulated deployments (the claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe yields guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 when all planned pairs (N=300) are included. We document a verified execution deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation. All execution, scoring, and validator artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/scoring/*.json) so every reported number is traceable.

sections.introduction: Autonomous, agentic pipelines that translate intent to network configurations promise operational efficiency but introduce an operational reliability problem: fluent LLM outputs may propose configuration changes that are syntactically plausible yet operationally unsafe. Systems‑level mitigations commonly proposed in the literature include deterministic validators, generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus, and human gating. Despite extensive conceptual work, there is a shortage of preregistered, artifact‑anchored, paired measurements that quantify (i) a model‑produced claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate in an operationally meaningful NetOps task bank and (ii) the empirical effect size of a guarded defense under a predeclared analysis plan. We designed and preregistered hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 to fill that gap. The run archived every model call, tool/validator trace, scoring decision, and analysis artifact with SHA‑256 checksums to make every numeric claim reproducible from the stored artifacts. The key contribution of this paper is (A) a fully archived paired measurement of LLM→action safety in a deterministic NetOps simulator and (B) a transparent accounting of a verified execution deviation (the preregistered ensemble was not executed) and of provider failures that materially affect inference.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps emphasizes intent‑to‑configuration translation, tool‑augmented agents, and validator‑assisted workflows. Deterministic verification research (NetKAT/SMT/HSAs) provides operationally meaningful validators for reachability and policy checks; recent LLM‑agent work advocates generate–validate–repair and constraint‑injection patterns. Taxonomies of agentic failure modes motivate conservative gating and independent verification. This experiment intentionally evaluates one practical defend‑and‑verify instantiation (deterministic validator + gate) under a preregistered paired design rather than attempting broad multi‑model generalization or an extensive ensemble comparison.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as hosted‑netops‑gvr‑v1‑2026‑08‑26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — the absolute paired difference in unsafe‑execution (claim→action) rates computed from paired binary outcomes per task. Confirmatory test: exact two‑sided McNemar plus paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Design and task generation. Deterministic generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial planned). Each task encodes an initial network state, an action safety policy, and a ground‑truth required sequence; task manifests and per‑task payloads are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl (see execution/execution_manifest.json for SHA‑256s). Execution contract. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Planned protocol: per task generate a shared initial candidate (one LLM generation), run the baseline evaluator (simulate executing the candidate), then run the guarded pipeline (preregistered: validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate). Preregistration set maximum_model_calls=600 and a single deterministic retry policy for failed provider calls. Validation and scoring. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parsed generated configuration text, normalized commands, executed them in an isolated deterministic simulator, and produced a binary safe/unsafe decision plus detailed validator_trace (validation_before/after states). These per‑episode scoring JSONs and raw responses are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/responses/*.txt; their SHA‑256s are in execution/execution_manifest.json. Primary analysis corpus: complete pairs with scorable binary outcomes for both baseline and guarded modes. Missingness and sensitivity plans. The preregistration specified treating only complete pairs as the primary confirmatory analysis and a preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe ('failure_as_unsafe') to bound conclusions when provider failures reduce effective N. All handling rules and exclusion criteria were frozen prior to execution and archived (preregistration). Deviation monitoring (audits). The execution manifest includes a provider_call audit and per‑call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json). The manifest records completed_hosted_model_call_event_count=273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count=28, and stage_counts ("shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1). These records permit deterministic reconciliation of observed outcomes to archived raw traces.
sections.results: Execution and raw provenance. Planned episodes: 600; completed episodes: 544; failed episodes: 56; model_calls_used: 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count: 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count: 28. The full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest and per‑episode artifacts are listed in execution/execution_manifest.json. Critical verified deviation (preregistered vs executed guarded pipeline). The preregistered guarded pipeline combined deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The archived execution shows only one shared_initial_generation per task and condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1} in the provider_call audit: the consensus ensemble stage was not executed. Therefore the guarded condition stored in the archive corresponds to deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation. This verified deviation is recorded by artifact paths and SHA‑256s in execution/execution_manifest.json and must be read into the interpretation below: the preregistered ensemble hypothesis was not tested by this run. Primary paired analysis (complete pairs). Complete analyzable pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 archived). Contingency (complete pairs): n11=271 (safe baseline & safe guarded), n10=1 (safe baseline & unsafe guarded), n01=0 (unsafe baseline & safe guarded), n00=0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294117647; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Interpretation: the observed discordant cell counts (n10=1, n01=0) yield an exact McNemar p = 1.0, providing no statistical evidence of a difference at conventional thresholds on the observed complete pairs. Missingness and conservative sensitivity. Missingness summary: complete_pairs=272; both_missing_pairs=28; failed_baseline_episodes=28; failed_guarded_episodes=28 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats all failed episodes as unsafe (failure_as_unsafe) on the full planned N=300 yields baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Failure provenance. The execution manifest and provider_call traces archive every failed call. The manifest records 28 failed hosted model calls; the detailed per‑call traces and timestamps are available under execution/provider_calls/*.json and the high‑level execution log is at execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA‑256s in execution/execution_manifest.json). Inspecting those archived traces is required to determine proximate causes (timeouts, API errors, network faults); the manifest contains the exact per‑call filenames and checksums to support independent auditing. Representative examples. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs and raw responses are archived; example artifact paths and SHA‑256s include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (sha256:465d73fd...) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (sha256:b227731a...) which show the normalized configuration candidate, validator_trace, and scoring decision used in the primary analysis. Reproducibility. All numbers above are computed from archived artifacts. The minimal artifact set to reproduce the primary analysis is: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, and execution/execution_manifest.json (all paths and SHA‑256s are present in the run archive). The execution and scoring JSONs permit re‑deriving every reported statistic deterministically.
sections.discussion: What the archived run demonstrates. Within the limits of the executed pipeline and the deterministic simulator, applying a deterministic validator to single LLM generations produced high per‑pair safety (near 100% on the analyzable pairs). However, the observed paired improvement is extremely small (~0.0037) and statistically inconclusive on the completed pairs (exact McNemar p = 1.0). Moreover, a material, verified deviation from the preregistered design (the consensus ensemble was not executed) prevents any artifact‑backed claim about ensemble effectiveness. The run therefore primarily documents (i) an artifact‑backed measurement of near‑perfect validator acceptance on analyzable pairs, (ii) substantial provider call failures that reduced effective N, and (iii) a concrete orchestration/deployment fragility that prevented execution of the preregistered ensemble. Threats to validity. Internal: single shared generation per paired episode (the designed independent seeded multiple draws for ensemble were not executed), provider reliability leading to missing pairs, and potential prompt sensitivity are important. Construct: the deterministic simulator and validator formalize operational safety but cannot capture every real deployment effect (timing, asymmetric traffic, hardware quirks). External: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic tasks, and an isolated simulator limit generalization to other models, larger task banks, or live equipment. Conclusion validity: the small observed absolute difference and low discordant counts give modest statistical power to detect small effects on the completed N=272; missingness exacerbates detectable‑effect size limitations. Operational implications. Deterministic validators can catch many straightforward misconfigurations in a controlled simulator; however, ensemble‑based defenses remain untested in this execution and provider reliability must be addressed to ensure robust measurement. The archived provider_call traces and execution logs fully document where orchestration or provider errors prevented preregistered operations and thus are necessary starting points for any engineering remediation. Recommendations for future runs. Reproduce the preregistered ensemble (three independent model draws + consensus) while improving orchestration and provider‑call robustness so the planned N=300 paired comparisons complete. Increase planned N to regain power lost to failed calls and run per‑prompt‑family stratified analyses to inspect robustness across benign/ambiguous/adversarial slices. Make the consensus stage deterministic (seeded draws archived separately per model) and retain per‑call provider traces as here.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired measurement of LLM→action safety and archived full execution, scoring, and analysis provenance. On 272 analyzable pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272 (absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0000,0.0110294]; McNemar p = 1.0). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls recorded) reduced effective N. We therefore release the full artifact bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json lists SHA‑256s for every per‑episode file) and recommend a re‑execution that both (A) runs the preregistered ensemble stage and (B) improves provider call robustness so the planned sample completes. All reported numbers and analysis artifacts cited above are stored in the run archive and reproducible from the listed files and checksums.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- Declared hosted model used in execution artifacts: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini").
- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (execution/scoring/*.json include validator_id and validator_version = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5").
- Exact initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. This immutable path+SHA‑256 is the required disclosure reference to the initial master prompt; the archived file provenance/master_prompt.txt is the canonical immutable record included in the run archive.
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 and a guarded defense consisting of a deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate.
- What actually executed (artifact evidence): execution/execution_manifest.json records planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Provider‑call audit fields show condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. Per‑episode response and scoring JSONs (execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json) and their SHA‑256s are archived and referenced in the execution manifest. These artifacts demonstrate that the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the guarded condition in the archived run therefore corresponded to the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a single shared generation. The preregistered consensus hypothesis was therefore not tested by this execution.
- Tools and capabilities permitted and used: deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), hosted LLM provider (declared gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and an isolated deterministic simulator used by the validator. All per‑call provider traces and validator traces were archived under execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/*.json and are included in the full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistration freeze and autonomy boundary: The preregistration was locked before observation (SHA‑256 above). After the autonomy lock the system autonomously generated tasks, executed model calls, validated configurations, scored outcomes, analyzed results, and drafted the manuscript; per‑step artifacts and hashes are archived. No human manual editing of technical content, numeric results, validator traces, figures, captions, references, or the Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock.
- Deviations and technical failures: A substantive, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered consensus ensemble stage was not executed; this is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and provider_call audits (stage_counts and condition_counts). Provider/model call failures produced 56 failed episodes (28 task pairs) that were excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis; this is recorded in analysis/missingness_summary.csv and execution/execution_log.jsonl. The preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') was applied and reported. All deviations, failures, and handling rules are archived and described in the manuscript.
- Human role: The human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock. After the lock all research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript text were generated autonomously; the provenance artifacts above document the autonomy boundary.
- Reproducibility pointers (artifact locations within the run archive): execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw responses), analysis/* (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg), execution/model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt (initial master prompt reference SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts show only a single shared_initial_generation per task). The executed guarded condition therefore functioned as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation; ensemble effects cannot be inferred from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
